title: WarHub Product Catalog
description: A consolidated or per-game-system product catalog document.

id.description: manufacturer-slug/product-code-or-name-slug. The suffix keeps the MANUFACTURER'S OWN CASING for a product code like CP01, MGKWB112, or 101010004SP; many contain uppercase letters, so this pattern is deliberately laxer than paint-catalog.json's all-lowercase one. The two catalogs have different id grammars ON PURPOSE: lowercasing product ids would break every supersedes/supersededBy pointer and every stored consumer link. Cross-catalog references therefore carry explicit id fields (paintIds/productIds) rather than assuming one shared shape. THE UNDERSCORE was added 2026-09-01: Sarissa Precision prints it in its own article numbers (B25A_R is the 25mm Round Acrylic base pack, B40x30A_O the 40x30mm Oval), and refusing it would have published those four as slugs of a shop's title instead of as the maker's code. It is URL-safe and it is the maker's spelling.

paintIds.description: Paint records sharing a barcode with this product -- the same physical thing published in the paint catalog too. Omitted when there is none. See barcode-index.json; ids are stable within a release.

settings.description: Labels of the SETTINGS -- universes or historical periods -- this product belongs to. For a product with gameSystems these are the settings those games are set in (see products/index.json, where each partition names its setting); a product with no game system can still carry one: a Black Library novel is set in Warhammer 40,000 and belongs to no game, a laser-cut Normandy farmhouse is a Second World War building however many WWII games sell it. Omitted when there is none.

weightG.description: NET CONTENTS in grams, for a product sold by mass rather than by volume (plastic glue, basing sand). Sibling of volumeMl; either, both or neither may be present. NOT a shipping weight. `minimum` mirrors this schema's own volumeMl rather than paint-catalog.json's unconstrained integer -- each side keeps its existing convention.
